exposure: largest myoma size (>= 5 cm vs. < 5 cm)
outcome: need for interventions (intrauterine Foley balloon, uterine artery embolization, hysterectomy)
cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women diagnosed with myoma who underwent cesarean myomectomy at Chungnam National University Hospital, comprising 77 singleton and 23 twin pregnancies.
finding: Cesarean myomectomy is a safe and effective procedure for both singleton and twin pregnancies, even in patients with large myomas.
mod_finding: The study confirmed that cesarean myomectomy is safe and effective when performed during a C-section for both singleton and twin pregnancies.
